---
title: "Introduction to Quality Assurance Process"
editor: visual
---


This analytical **Quality Assurance** (QA) process is designed to ensure we have consistency in the way that analysis and outputs are assured for accuracy, reliability and value.

It is designed to be light-touch: there are clear principles that apply to everything we do, and with a proportionate approach.

The principles should be applied to all work, although the level of input and sign-off required is based on a tiered, risk-based assessment.

It is important to ensure that there is a clear distinction between level of process (High/Medium/Low) and assurance of the outputs (Gold/Silver/Bronze).

### Process

With regards to the process it will help to ensure products:

- Met the requirements set out

- Are contextual and aligned with wider priorities and factors

- Are representative of our team’s identity, and contribute effectively to the sum of our output

- Provide the most value possible

- Can be maintained or reproduced with resilience

### Outputs

With regards to the outputs it will help to ensure that:

- The accuracy and any limitations are known

- The degree of reliability the analysis has is known

- The level of confidence in using this analysis a stakeholder should have is known

- This process is expected to evolve over time and will flex and adapt as required
